The authors applied label smoothing with a value of ϵₗₛ = 0.1 [1][2]. They note that this hurts perplexity because the model becomes more uncertain, but it improves accuracy and the BLEU score [1][2].

The Transformer encodes positions with sinusoidal functions: each dimension uses a sine or cosine of the form PE(pos, 2i) = sin(pos / 10000^{2i/d_model}) and PE(pos, 2i+1) = cos(pos / 10000^{2i/d_model})【1】.

RAG‑Sequence treats the retrieved passage as a single latent variable and uses the same document to generate every token of the output sequence, marginalizing over the top‑K documents only once per answer [3].  
RAG‑Token, in contrast, allows a different retrieved document to be drawn for each target token, marginalizing separately for each token so the generator can draw content from multiple documents when producing an answer [2][3].

Thorough Decoding is a decoding procedure for RAG‑Sequence in which, after generating a candidate set Y of hypotheses, an additional forward pass is run for each document z that did not produce a given hypothesis y in its beam; the generator probability for y is multiplied by the retrieval probability pη(z|x) and these products are summed across all documents to obtain the marginal probability of y [1][2].

BEIR reports Normalised Cumulative Discount Gain (nDCG@k) as the evaluation metric for all datasets [1].

The BEIR benchmark finds that BM25 remains a strong baseline: many models that beat BM25 on in‑domain data fail to generalize and under‑perform BM25 on the zero‑shot BEIR datasets, while approaches that consistently outperform BM25 (e.g., cross‑attentional re‑ranking, ColBERT, docT5query) are highlighted as generally robust across tasks【3】.
Re‑ranking and late‑interaction architectures obtain the highest zero‑shot performance on the BEIR benchmark, but they incur high computational costs【4】.

TAS‑B is a dense‑retrieval model evaluated in the BEIR benchmark that achieves the strongest zero‑shot generalization among dense approaches, outperforming ANCE and DPR on most datasets. The WikiEval dataset was built by first picking 50 Wikipedia pages about events that occurred since the start of 2022, giving preference to pages that had recent edits. For each page, the authors asked ChatGPT to generate a question that could be fully answered from the page’s introductory section, using a prompt that required the question to be non‑trivial, moderately difficult, and answerable from the context. They then had ChatGPT answer each generated question using the same introductory text, and finally two fluent English annotators labeled every question‑context‑answer triple along the three quality dimensions of faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance【2†L1-L9】【2†L10-L13】.
